name: Jain Dal Tadka
description: Smooth yellow lentils tempered with cumin, asafoetida and tomato, made without onion or garlic.
steps: Wash the dal and boil it with water, turmeric and salt for 20-25 minutes until soft. Whisk lightly.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 10 seconds.
Add asafoetida and slit green chilli, then the chopped tomatoes and chilli powder.
Cook for 4-5 minutes until the tomatoes turn soft and mushy.
Pour the tempering into the dal, simmer for 3 minutes and garnish with coriander leaves.
tips: Asafoetida gives the savory depth that onion and garlic normally provide.
Add hot water if the dal thickens.
substitutions: Use masoor dal for a faster cook of about 15 minutes.

name: Lauki Sabzi
description: Tender bottle gourd cooked simply with tomato, cumin and a hint of lemon.
steps: Peel the bottle gourd and cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, asafoetida and chopped green chilli.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder and salt. Cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the bottle gourd and mix well. Cover and cook on low for 12-15 minutes, stirring now and then. It releases its own water, so add none.
Finish with garam masala and lemon juice.
tips: Do not add water. The gourd cooks in its own moisture.
Choose a young, firm gourd. Older ones turn bitter.
substitutions: Use ridge gourd or zucchini in place of bottle gourd.

name: Cabbage Sabzi
description: A quick dry stir-fry of cabbage and peas with mustard seeds and turmeric.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and wait for them to pop. Add cumin seeds, asafoetida and slit green chillies.
Add the peas, turmeric and salt and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and sugar. Toss on medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes, uncovered, until tender but still slightly crunchy.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves.
tips: Keep the pan uncovered so the cabbage roasts and does not turn watery.
Do not overcook. It should keep a little bite.
substitutions: Add a handful of roasted peanuts for crunch, unless you avoid peanuts.

name: Tindora Sabzi
description: Ivy gourd stir-fried with mustard, turmeric and a touch of jaggery.
steps: Wash the tindora, trim the ends and slice lengthwise into thin strips.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let them pop. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Add the tindora, turmeric and salt. Mix well.
Cover and cook on low for 10-12 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Add coriander powder, chilli powder and sugar. Cook uncovered for 3-4 minutes until slightly crisp. Finish with lemon juice.
tips: Thin slices cook evenly and get crisp edges.
Add the spice powders at the end so they do not burn.
substitutions: Use okra or ridge gourd if tindora is not available.

name: Coconut Moong Dal
description: Creamy yellow lentils simmered with coconut and finished with a mustard and curry leaf tempering.
steps: Wash the dal and boil it with water and turmeric for 20 minutes until completely soft.
Grind the coconut and green chillies with a little water into a paste.
Add the paste and salt to the dal. Simmer for 5 minutes, adding hot water if too thick.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and when they pop add dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Pour the tempering over the dal and serve with rice.
tips: Do not boil hard after adding the coconut paste.
Serve with rice and a dry vegetable for a full meal.
substitutions: Use 3 tbsp of desiccated coconut soaked in warm water if fresh coconut is unavailable.

name: Vegetable Stew
description: Mild Kerala-style stew of mixed vegetables in thin coconut milk with whole spices.
steps: Heat oil and add cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. Let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add sliced onion, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves. Cook for 3-4 minutes without browning.
Add the vegetables, water and salt. Cover and cook for 12-15 minutes until tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and black pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Do not boil hard.
Serve with appam, idli or rice.
tips: Keep the onion pale. The stew should be white and mild.
Boiling coconut milk hard can make it split.
substitutions: Add cubed potato for a heartier stew, unless you avoid potatoes.

name: Tomato Rasam
description: A thin, peppery, tangy South Indian soup of tomato, tamarind and spices.
steps: Pressure cook the dal with turmeric and 1 cup of water until very soft. Mash it.
Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the pulp.
Crush the pepper and half the cumin coarsely.
Boil the chopped tomatoes with the tamarind pulp, 2 cups of water, salt and the crushed spices for 8-10 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the mashed dal and simmer for 3 minutes. Do not boil hard.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, dried chillies, curry leaves, asafoetida and the remaining cumin. Pour over the rasam and add coriander leaves.
tips: Rasam should be thin and fragrant, so do not thicken it.
Serve hot with rice or sip it as a soup.
substitutions: Use 1 tbsp lemon juice instead of tamarind, added at the end.

name: Besan Chilla
description: Savory gram flour pancakes with tomato and coriander, a quick high-protein breakfast.
steps: Whisk the besan, water, turmeric, chilli powder, ajwain and salt into a smooth, pourable batter with no lumps.
Stir in finely chopped tomato, green chilli and coriander leaves.
Heat a non-stick pan on medium and grease lightly. Pour a ladle of batter and spread it into a round.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is golden. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.
Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes more. Serve hot.
tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes for softer chillas.
Spread thin for crisp edges, thicker for soft ones.
substitutions: Add grated cabbage or spinach to the batter for extra vegetables.

name: Chana Sundal
description: A light, protein-rich chickpea salad tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves and coconut.
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight. Pressure cook with salt for 6-7 whistles until soft but whole. Drain well.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and when they pop add dried chillies, green chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Add the chickpeas and toss for 2-3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, add the grated coconut and lemon juice, and mix.
tips: Drain the chickpeas completely so the sundal stays dry.
Serve warm as a snack.
substitutions: Use two cans of chickpeas, drained and rinsed, to skip the soaking.

name: Sev Tamatar
description: A tangy, lightly sweet tomato curry topped with crunchy sev, a Gujarati favourite.
steps: Chop the tomatoes finely.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they pop add asafoetida and slit green chillies.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sugar and salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates.
Add the water and simmer for 5 minutes to make a thin gravy.
Pour into a bowl, top with sev and coriander leaves, and serve immediately.
tips: Add the sev just before eating so it stays crisp.
A little sugar balances the sourness of the tomatoes.
substitutions: Use crushed papdi or plain boondi if you have no sev.

name: Matar Pulao
description: Light basmati rice cooked with green peas and whole spices.
steps: Wash the rice until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon. Let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add slit green chillies and the peas and stir for 1 minute.
Add the rice and fry gently for 1 minute. Add water and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12-15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
tips: Do not stir once the lid is on.
Frozen peas can go in directly.
substitutions: Add cauliflower florets or beans for a mixed vegetable version.

name: Ragi Dosa
description: Quick, crisp finger-millet crepes that need no fermentation, with a simple tempering.
steps: Mix the ragi flour, rice flour, chopped chillies, cumin, curry leaves, coriander leaves and salt in a bowl.
Add the water and whisk into a thin, runny batter, thinner than regular dosa batter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a flat pan on medium-high and grease it lightly.
Stir the batter, then pour it from a height in a ring shape, starting from the outside and filling the centre.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 2-3 minutes until crisp. Flip only if needed and serve hot.
tips: The batter must stay thin, so stir it before every dosa because the flour settles.
The pan must be hot or the dosa sticks.
substitutions: Add finely chopped onion if you do not follow Jain rules.

name: Tomato Rice
description: Tangy, spiced rice cooked with tomato, mustard seeds and curry leaves.
steps: Spread the cooked rice on a plate to cool so the grains separate.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and chana dal. When the seeds pop and the dal turns golden, add dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes turn into a thick, oily paste.
Add the rice and mix gently on low heat for 2-3 minutes so every grain is coated.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
tips: Cook the tomato until the oil separates. This gives the dish its depth.
Day-old rice works best.
substitutions: Add a squeeze of lemon at the end if the tomatoes are not sour enough.

name: Vagharelo Khichdi
description: Soft rice and moong dal khichdi finished with a fragrant mustard and cumin tempering.
steps: Wash the rice and dal together and soak for 15 minutes. Drain.
Pressure cook with the water, turmeric and salt for 3-4 whistles until soft and mushy.
Let the pressure release naturally and mix well. Add hot water to adjust the consistency.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they pop add asafoetida, dried chilli, green chilli and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the khichdi and serve hot.
tips: Khichdi thickens as it cools. Add hot water when reheating.
Serve with pickle or papad.
substitutions: Add peas or bottle gourd cubes for extra vegetables.

name: Rava Uttapam
description: Soft, thick semolina pancakes topped with tomato, chilli and coriander.
steps: Mix the rava, water, cumin, pepper and salt into a thick batter. Rest for 15 minutes so the rava swells.
Chop the tomato, chillies and coriander leaves finely.
Heat a non-stick pan on medium and grease lightly. Pour a ladle of batter and spread it into a thick round.
Sprinkle the toppings and press them in gently. Drizzle oil around the edge.
Cook covered for 2-3 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more until golden.
tips: Resting the batter is essential, or the uttapam turns gritty.
Add a splash of water if the batter thickens while resting.
substitutions: Add grated carrot or capsicum on top for more vegetables, unless you follow Jain rules.
